_source: Recovered verbatim from 'Shawn Ryder Digital.dc.html' (v1). The v2 file exceeded the 256 KiB design-API read cap and was truncated mid-renderVals(), taking its copies of these arrays with it. v2 may have revised this wording — worth a read-through before launch.

services.title: Local SEO & Google Business Profile
services.blurb: When someone searches your brand plus your city, you should own that page. Most stores don’t.
services.long: Your Google Business Profile does more selling than most of your website. I get it filled out properly, posted to consistently, and ranking in the local pack for the searches that actually end in a visit — not vanity keywords.
items: Local pack rank tracking by model line

services.title: Social media content
services.blurb: Real content from your lot, in your voice — not stock photos of cars you don’t stock.
services.long: Dealership social works when it looks like your store, not a template. I build a simple monthly rhythm your team can actually keep up with: units on the lot, delivery photos, staff, service specials, community stuff.

services.title: Email marketing
services.blurb: Your database is the cheapest inventory of buyers you own. Most dealers ignore it.
services.long: Equity mining, service-to-sales, lease maturity, sold-customer follow-up. Emails written like a person wrote them, sent on a schedule, measured on appointments — not open rates.

services.title: Reputation management
services.blurb: One angry review at the top of your profile costs more than any ad you’re running.
services.long: A steady ask process for happy customers, fast honest responses to the unhappy ones, and a score that reflects how your store actually treats people.
items: Review request process for sales and service

services.title: Full-service digital retainer
services.blurb: Hand me the whole stack and stop coordinating five vendors.
services.long: Search, social, email, reputation, website content and lead-follow-up process under one roof, with one person accountable. You get a monthly plan, the work done, and a plain-language report on what it produced.

diffs: 25 years in and around the automotive business
Retail sales and dealership operations experience
You talk to me — not an account coordinator
Plain-language reporting you can read in five minutes

steps.title: The audit
steps.body: I go through your site, Google profile, reviews and lead response like a shopper would, then tell you the honest version of what I find.

steps.title: The plan
steps.body: One page. What we fix first, what it should produce, what it costs. No 40-slide deck, no jargon.

steps.title: The work
steps.body: I execute, you sell cars. Monthly check-in on what moved and what we’re changing next.

beliefs.p: Speed to lead beats every clever campaign. If your follow-up is broken, fixing ads is a waste of money.
Reputation travels fast in a local market. Treating reviews as marketing — not admin — pays for itself.
A process your team will actually run every day outperforms the platform nobody logs into.
Impressions don’t hit a forecast. Appointments, shows and deliveries do.
